text:
marta: Seeing a ~25% token/sec drop across the us-west batcher fleet since canary-4 rolled. Latency p50 up ~12%, p95 up ~40%. No obvious infra flaps. Suspect scheduler preemption change from the kernel-selection PR interacting with small-batch heuristics.
ajay: ugh. can you paste perf graphs? which metric shows the drop?
marta: token/sec aggregated per-pod metric: https://grafana/redwood/d/xyz/batcher?orgId=1&from=now-2h&to=now — sharp step down at 10:47 with canary deploy. heatmap shows more 1-2 token batches and increased queue_wait_ms.
leo: did the PR change the preemption window or add aggressive preemption for kernels that take longer? I remember a tweak to prefer lower-latency kernels which sometimes preempts in-flight small batches.
marta: yep, PR #9832 changed kernel hinting to prefer fused attention kernel for long sequences and added: `if estimated_latency > preempt_threshold && pending_small_batches > 0 then preempt=true` — looks like that.
kris: deploy-bot: Canary-4 deployed to us-west-2 at 2026-03-04T10:47:12Z :rocket:
ci-bot: perf-check: batcher_token_rate regression detected on canary-4 vs baseline (p < 0.01). See CI run 2026-03-04-1187.
ajay: can we repro locally with load test? marta, can you share a captured trace from a pod? kv-cache hitrate looked stable?
marta: attached flamegraph (s3://perf/trace-1855021234.svg) and a small log snippet: ```
[10:46:59] batcher: accept request id=abc seq_len=32
[10:46:59] scheduler: queued request id=abc wait_ms=5
[10:47:00] batcher: preempting batch id=42 for kernel=fused_attn est_lat=18.2 preempt_threshold=15.0
[10:47:00] batcher: dispatch small batch id=43 size=1 -> kernel=fast_gemm
[10:47:00] kernel: <fused_attn> warmup 30ms
[10:47:01] kvcache: evict key=usr-123 front=0 ttl=300ms (hitrate 0.72->0.69)
```
leo: interesting the preempt log shows preempting for fused_attn -> warmup penalty causing more small batches to run alone. That would reduce token/sec due to lost batching opportunities.
kris: can someone run the binary with `--sched-debug=1` and `--preempt-window-ms=0` to check behaviour? maybe disabling preemption temporarily for small batches is low risk.
ajay: running a local load test now with canary build and with preempt-window set to 0. Also toggling `batch_min_coalesce_ms` from 4 -> 8 to allow more coalescing.
ajay: quick repro: with default flags token/sec 8200, with `--preempt-window-ms=0` token/sec 10750. That's near baseline (10860). So preemption seems causal.
marta: thanks. can we bisect which change in #9832 introduced the behavior? PR had two commits: kernel-selection heuristics + preemption flag. If we revert the preemption commit only we might fix without losing kernel hinting.
leo: agree. low-risk revert: revert commit 7b1c4a (preemption condition). I'll open a revert PR and push to canary-4 hold.
leo: PR #9901 opened to revert preemption logic. requesting review @ajay @kris.
kris: adding rollout hold: we should pause further canaries. deploy-bot: Rollout hold applied to canary-channel at 2026-03-04T11:03:12Z.
ci-bot: perf-smoke: running perf job for revert PR #9901 (baseline compare).
ajay: also adding a temporary scheduler flag guard (`--enable-preemption=false`) controlled via config so we can flip without deploys. I'll push config toggle to staging.
leo: merged #9901 to canary-channel rollback branch and triggered canary deploy. deploy-bot: Canary revert deployed at 2026-03-04T11:21:45Z.
kris: monitoring... token/sec climbing back. current aggregate token/sec ~10690, p95 latency improving.
marta: kv-cache hitrate recovered to 0.73. queue_wait_ms dropped. Looks like revert fixes.
ajay: leaving the small-coalesce change (8 ms) as a tweak in a separate PR to improve batching margin.
leo: follow-up actions: 1) add a regression test in CI that simulates small-batch heavy traffic and asserts token/sec within 95% of baseline; 2) add telemetry counters for preempt events (per-kernel, per-sequence-length); 3) document the kernel warmup penalty in the kernel-selection README.
kris: thanks team. I'll keep the rollout hold until tomorrow morning and schedule a short postmortem. tagging #eng-runtime. :thumbsup:
marta: great catch everyone. saved a bunch of customer calls.
ajay: adding the perf graphs and the repro commands to the PR.
